name: Prop handoff

intent.purpose: Establish the geography and the key as the shared object of the scene.
intent.reason: The audience must see that the key starts between them before anyone claims it.
intent.attention: The red key on the bench, then Tess's right hand lifting it.
intent.relationships: Tess controls the key and Arlo waits; the balance of power rests with her.

staging.positions: Tess and Arlo stand on opposite sides of the workbench with the key centered between them.
staging.facing: They face each other across the bench.
staging.eyelines: Both look down at the key, then Arlo's eyes follow it up as Tess lifts it.
staging.movement: Tess reaches and lifts the key with her right hand. Arlo stays still.
staging.camera: Static or near-static side-on two-shot at bench height, keeping both figures and the key readable.

editorial.cutIn: The scene opens on this composition.
editorial.cutOut: Cut once the key is raised and held, moving from the open two-shot to a tighter single on Tess as she speaks.
editorial.timing: Let the key sit for a beat before the pickup so its importance registers.

advanced.continuity: The key is in Tess's right hand at the end and stays there into the next shot.
advanced.assumptions: The side-on camera and opposite-side positions are staging assumptions; the script says only that the key lies between them.

shots.title: Key Between Them
shots.sourceExcerpt:
## INT. WORKSHOP - DAY

A red key rests on the workbench between Tess and Arlo. Tess picks it up in her right hand.
shots.description: Opening: a balanced medium-wide two-shot across the workbench. Tess and Arlo stand on opposite sides, and the red key rests on the bench centered between them. After a held beat, Tess reaches out and picks up the key in her right hand. Ending: Tess holds the key at chest height, still in the two-shot, and Arlo watches it.
shots.atmosphere: Daytime workshop, still and attentive. Quiet room tone.
shots.music: None; let the room tone carry the pause.

intent.purpose: Deliver the single condition attached to the key.
intent.reason: The line is the scene's only spoken information and deserves Tess's face.
intent.attention: Tess's expression as she speaks, with the key in frame as a reminder.
intent.relationships: Tess entrusts and sets terms; Arlo is the one being trusted.

staging.positions: The same positions across the workbench.
staging.eyelines: Tess looks toward Arlo, slightly off-lens on the side of his shoulder.
staging.movement: Minimal. Tess keeps the key in her right hand.
staging.camera: Over-the-shoulder from Arlo's side, framing Tess in a medium close-up.

editorial.cutIn: Cut in on the raised key and Tess's intent to speak.
editorial.cutOut: Cut after her held look, into the physical handover.
editorial.timing: Leave a short silence after the line before cutting.

advanced.continuity: The key stays in Tess's right hand, and her eyeline matches Arlo's side of the bench.
advanced.assumptions: The over-the-shoulder placement is a staging choice and is not specified in the script.

shots.title: Before Dark
shots.sourceExcerpt:
### TESS

Bring it back before dark.
shots.description: Opening: a medium close-up of Tess over Arlo's soft-focus shoulder, with the red key visible in her right hand at the lower edge of the frame. Clearly tighter and more angled than the previous two-shot. Tess looks at Arlo and delivers her line evenly. Ending: Tess holds her look on Arlo after the line, and the key is still in her hand.
shots.atmosphere: Intimate and direct. The condition carries weight.

intent.purpose: Show the transfer of the key clearly and completely.
intent.reason: The handover is the scene's central action and reads best close on the hands.
intent.attention: The red key moving from Tess's right hand to Arlo's left palm, then into his pocket.
intent.relationships: Responsibility passes physically from Tess to Arlo.

staging.positions: Hands meet over the workbench between them.
staging.facing: Not applicable; the frame isolates the hands.
staging.eyelines: Off-screen; both characters' attention is implied on the key.
staging.movement: Tess places the key, Arlo closes his left hand, then pockets it on his left side.
staging.camera: A close insert that tilts or pans with Arlo's left hand to the pocket.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from Tess's held look to the hands as she acts on her words.
editorial.cutOut: Cut once the key is pocketed, back to Tess and what remains.
editorial.timing: Unhurried; give each step of the transfer its own moment.

advanced.continuity: The giving hand is Tess's right, the receiving hand Arlo's open left palm, and the pocket is on Arlo's left side.
advanced.assumptions: The camera's follow move is a staging choice; the hand and side details come from the script.

shots.title: Into His Palm
shots.sourceExcerpt: She places it in Arlo’s open left palm. He closes his hand and pockets the key on his left side. Tess looks at the now empty patch of workbench.
shots.description: Opening: a close insert over the workbench at hand level, showing Arlo's open left palm held out and Tess's right hand bringing the red key toward it, with no faces in frame. Tess places the key in his palm. Arlo closes his hand around it. The camera follows his closed left hand as he draws it back and slips the key into a pocket on his left side. Ending: a close frame on Arlo's left side as his hand leaves the pocket, with the key now out of sight.
shots.atmosphere: Tactile and deliberate. The quiet sounds of hand and pocket.

intent.purpose: Close the scene on what Tess has let go of.
intent.reason: The script ends on her look at the empty spot, which carries the emotional aftertaste.
intent.attention: Tess's downward gaze and the empty patch of workbench.
intent.relationships: Tess now has nothing in her hands, and her trust is in Arlo's keeping.

staging.positions: Tess stays at the workbench. Arlo remains present but out of frame or at the frame edge.
staging.eyelines: Tess looks down at the empty patch where the key lay.
staging.movement: Tess's gaze drops; no other significant movement.
staging.camera: A static medium shot with the bench surface prominent in the foreground.

editorial.cutIn: Cut from the pocketed key to Tess, completing the action's emotional consequence.
editorial.cutOut: The scene ends on Tess's held look at the empty bench.
editorial.timing: Hold long enough for the absence to register.

advanced.continuity: The key's former spot on the bench must match its position in the first shot, and Tess's hands are empty.
advanced.assumptions: Whether Arlo appears in this frame is a staging choice; the script says only that he is present in the scene.

shots.title: The Empty Patch
shots.sourceExcerpt: She places it in Arlo’s open left palm. He closes his hand and pockets the key on his left side. Tess looks at the now empty patch of workbench.
shots.description: Opening: a medium shot of Tess on her side of the workbench, framed wider than the hand insert and clearly distinct from it, with the bench surface in the foreground. Her hand is now empty. She lowers her gaze to the now empty patch of workbench where the key had rested. Ending: Tess looks down at the bare patch of bench, which sits in the foreground of the frame.
shots.atmosphere: A quiet afterbeat. The room settles around the absence.

strategies.dramaticProgression: A quiet handover of trust. Tess takes the red key, sets a single condition, and gives it to Arlo. The scene ends on what she has given up, with her looking at the empty spot where the key lay.
strategies.visualProgression: Open with an even two-shot that sets the key between them as shared, neutral ground. Move to Tess for the condition. Close in on the hands for the transfer. End on Tess and the empty workbench, so the frame shifts from shared object to her sense of loss.
strategies.audienceInformation: The audience learns that the key matters and must return before dark. It never learns what the key opens or why the deadline matters. Coverage keeps that unknown intact by staying on the key and the gesture rather than explaining.
strategies.spatialAnchors: The workbench sits between Tess and Arlo with the red key on it. Tess uses her right hand. Arlo receives with his open left palm and pockets on his left side. The patch of bench where the key lay is the final anchor.
